Duality (category theory)

Words: 34
Category OurBigBook.com
Reversing the arrows in a categorical statement produces its dual statement. A theorem holding for all categories therefore has a dual theorem obtained by applying it to the opposite category; for example, categorical limits are exchanged with colimits.

Morphism in a category (f:A→B)

Words: 62
Category OurBigBook.com
A categorical morphism is an arrow with a specified source and target in a category. An arrow f:A→B composes with g:B→C to give gf:A→C. Composition is associative, and every object has an identity arrow acting as a unit. A functor preserves the sources, targets, identities and compositions of these arrows. In a locally small category, the arrows between fixed objects form a hom-set.

Small projective object (E(A,−) preserves all small colimits)

Words: 65
Category OurBigBook.com
An object with the displayed property is called small projective; the term 0-presentable here uses this all-small-colimits convention. In a presheaf category, every representable presheaf has this property by the Yoneda lemma and pointwise computation of colimits. Conversely the canonical colimit presentation of a presheaf shows that the identity on such an object factors through one representable, making it a retract. If the indexing category has equalizers, a representable retract is again representable by the representable retract criterion.

Category of small categories (Cat)

Words: 149 Articles: 3
Category OurBigBook.com
Objects are small categories and morphisms are functors. Its products pair objects and arrows componentwise. Its exponential objects are functor categories, as shown by the currying adjunction for small categories.

Indiscrete category

Words: 29
Category of small categories OurBigBook.com
The indiscrete category on a set has exactly one morphism between each ordered pair of objects. Every morphism is invertible. A functor into it is determined by its object assignment.

Discrete category

Words: 27
Category of small categories OurBigBook.com
The discrete category on a set has that set as its objects and only identity morphisms. Functors from it are exactly assignments of objects in the target category.

Free category on independent arrows (L(S)=∐s∈S​[1])

Words: 73
Category of small categories OurBigBook.com
Take two distinct objects and one nonidentity arrow for each element of S, without arrows between different copies. A functor from this category to C is exactly a choice of one arbitrary arrow of C for each element of S. Consequently this construction is left adjoint to the functor taking the set of all arrows of a small category. Its free object has three arrows per generator, including the two identity arrows.

Preadditive category

Words: 38
Category OurBigBook.com
A category is preadditive if every hom-set is an abelian group and composition is additive in each variable. Zero morphisms and differences of parallel morphisms are therefore defined. A zero object or finite biproducts need not exist; these are extra requirements in an additive category.

Coreflective subcategory (I⊣q)

Words: 54
Category OurBigBook.com
A full subcategory is coreflective when its inclusion I has a right adjoint q. The counit IqX→X is universal for maps to X from objects of the subcategory. The comonad Iq is idempotent. For a finite-limit-closed coreflective subcategory of a topos, its coalgebra construction can prove that the subcategory is itself a topos.

Generating set in a category ((Pi​)i∈I​)

Words: 31
Category OurBigBook.com
A generating set is a set-indexed family (Pi​) such that unequal parallel morphisms f,g:A→B are distinguished by some h:Pi​→A, with fh=gh. It is dual to a cogenerating set.

Composition in a category (g∘f)

Words: 21
Category OurBigBook.com
Given morphisms f:A→B and g:B→C, their composite is gf:A→C. Composition is associative and has the identity morphisms as units.

Object of a category

Words: 15
Category OurBigBook.com
The objects are the entities between which a category specifies morphisms. Each object has an identity morphism.

Terminal category (1)

Words: 19
Category OurBigBook.com
The category with one object and only its identity morphism. A functor from it selects an object of the target category.

Nested partial unary operation category (Cn​)

Words: 228 Articles: 2
Category OurBigBook.com
An object of Cn​ is a set with a finite list of partial unary operations. The first is total; the domain of each later operation consists exactly of the defined fixed points of the immediately preceding operation. Morphisms preserve every defined operation. Take C0​ to be the Category of sets. This tower gives examples of arbitrary finite monadic length even though its long free–forgetful composites induce the same first monad.

Free extension of nested partial unary operations (Fn​⊣Gn​)

Words: 164 Articles: 1
Nested partial unary operation category OurBigBook.com
For an object of the nested partial unary operation category Cn​, adjoining the next operation freely gives one new value at each defined fixed point of the previous operation. Each new value starts an infinite free chain under the first unary operation; the other old operations are undefined on those new points. The new top operation consequently has no fixed points, so subsequent free extensions add no points. This gives a left adjoint to forgetting the last operation; extensions of maps along the chains are forced by the first target operation.

Split-coequalizer lifting for a fixed-point-domain operation (βQ​(z)=qβB​(sz))

Words: 78
Free extension of nested partial unary operations OurBigBook.com
In the nested partial unary operation category, suppose the lower-operation diagram A⇉Bq​Q has a split coequalizer with qs=1, ft=1 and gt=sq. The section s takes eligible fixed points to eligible fixed points, so the displayed next operation is defined on exactly the required domain. For eligible x∈B, the equations give
qβB​(x)=qfβA​(tx)=qgβA​(tx)=qβB​(sqx).
(1)
Thus q preserves the next operation. Every factored morphism preserves it by evaluating at sz, giving creation of the specified coequalizer. Together with reflection of isomorphisms, the Beck monadicity theorem proves one-step monadicity.

Coseparator

Words: 173 Articles: 3
Category OurBigBook.com
A coseparator S in a category distinguishes parallel arrows by postcomposition: if u=v:X→B, some t:B→S satisfies tu=tv. Equivalently, the contravariant functor C(−,S) is faithful. In a complete category that is a locally small category, the evaluation arrow B→∏t∈C(B,S)​S is a monomorphism.

Cogenerating set ((Qi​)i∈I​)

Words: 77 Articles: 1
Coseparator OurBigBook.com
A cogenerating set is a set-indexed family (Qi​)i∈I​ such that whenever f=g:A→B, there is a morphism q:B→Qi​ with qf=qg. It generalizes a single coseparator. In a locally small category with the needed products in a category, it gives an evaluation embedding into cogenerator products.

Evaluation embedding into cogenerator products

Words: 37
Cogenerating set OurBigBook.com
For a small cogenerating family (Qi​) in a locally small category, the evaluation arrow C→∏i,q∈C(C,Qi​)​Qi​ is a monomorphism whenever that small product in a category exists. Equality after all its projections is equality after every map to a cogenerator, hence equality of the original parallel morphisms.

Equalizer presentation by powers of a coseparator (B⟶SI⇉SJ)

Words: 53
Coseparator OurBigBook.com
In a complete category that is a locally small category with a coseparator S, suppose every monomorphism is a regular monomorphism. The evaluation embedding B→SI, I=C(B,S), is an equalizer of some pair into Q. Composing that pair with the evaluation embedding Q→SJ leaves the equalizer unchanged. Here powers mean products in a category indexed by sets, without assuming an exponential object exists.

Category of rings (Rng)

Words: 56
Category OurBigBook.com
The category of unital rings has identity-preserving ring homomorphisms as morphisms. The zero ring, allowing 0=1, is terminal, and Z is initial. Nonzero rings admit no maps from the zero ring. Monomorphisms are injective: maps from Z[x] probe individual elements. It is a regular category, with surjective homomorphisms as regular epimorphisms; these are distinct from arbitrary categorical epimorphisms.

Skeletal category

Words: 126 Articles: 1
Category OurBigBook.com
A skeletal category has no distinct isomorphic objects. A full and faithful functor with essential surjectivity between two skeletal categories is an isomorphism of categories: surjectivity on isomorphism classes becomes surjectivity on objects, and faithfulness and fullness reflect an equality of image objects to an isomorphism, hence an equality, of source objects.

Skeleton of a category

Words: 83
Skeletal category OurBigBook.com
A skeleton of C is a full subcategory with exactly one object from each isomorphism class. The axiom of choice supplies skeletons of small categories. Conversely, if every small category has a skeletal equivalent, apply this to the groupoid on ∐i​Ai​ with exactly one morphism between objects in the same nonempty fibre. Let F:C→D, G:D→C, η:1⇒GF and ε:FG⇒1 be natural transformations. If GεηG​=1G​, then e=εF​Fη:F⇒F is an idempotent morphism in the functor category. Naturality implies Geη=η and εeG​=ε; these absorption identities prove e2=e. The omitted triangle measures exactly whether e=1F​.
Splitting a one-triangle adjunction idempotent
Words: 60
One-triangle adjunction idempotent OurBigBook.com
The one-triangle adjunction idempotent splits if and only if G has a left adjoint. From a splitting Fr​Hs​F, define the new unit Grη and counit εsG​; the absorption identities imply both triangle identities for an adjunction. Conversely, for H⊣G with unit ψ:1⇒GH and counit φ:HG⇒1, the splitting maps are r=εH​Fψ and s=φF​Hη. Their composites are rs=1H​ and sr=e.

Fully faithful adjoint criterion

Words: 78 Articles: 1
Unit and counit of an adjunction OurBigBook.com
For F⊣G, the right adjoint G is full and faithful exactly when the counit FG→1 is an isomorphism. Dually, F is full and faithful exactly when the unit 1→GF is an isomorphism.
Double-adjoint comparison transformation (θ)
Words: 43
Fully faithful adjoint criterion OurBigBook.com
For F⊣G⊣H with full and faithful G, write η,ε for the first unit and counit and α,β for the second. The two composites
HHη​HGF(αF)−1​F,H(εH)−1​FGHFβ​F
(16)
coincide. Their common value is the double-adjoint comparison transformation H→F.

Faithful left adjoint criterion

Words: 34
Unit and counit of an adjunction OurBigBook.com
For F⊣G, the left adjoint F is faithful exactly when every unit component ηA​:A→GFA is a monomorphism. Under the adjunction, equality after ηA​ corresponds precisely to equality after applying F.

Pointwise-monic unit-and-counit criterion

Words: 111 Articles: 1
Unit and counit of an adjunction OurBigBook.com
Suppose C is balanced and every morphism of D factors as a strong epimorphism followed by a monomorphism. For F:C⇄D:G, both unit and counit are pointwise monic exactly when F is full and faithful and its essential image is closed under strong quotients.
Pointwise-monic adjunction over a non-balanced poset
Words: 64
Pointwise-monic unit-and-counit criterion OurBigBook.com
Let C={0<1} and let D be the terminal category. The unique functor F:C→D is left adjoint to the functor selecting 1. Every arrow in a poset is monic, so the unit and counit are pointwise monic, but F is not full because the unique arrow F1→F0 has no preimage 1→0. The category C is not balanced.

Adjoint functor theorem for complete lattices

Words: 29
Adjoint functors OurBigBook.com
For complete lattices, a monotone map f:A→B preserves arbitrary joins exactly when it has a right adjoint. In that case
f∗(b)=⋁{a∈A:f(a)≤b},f(a)≤b⟺a≤f∗(b).
(17)

Right Kan extension

Words: 35
Adjoint functors OurBigBook.com
The right Kan extension along K:C→D is the right adjoint to precomposition by K between suitable functor categories.
This is the right-adjoint form of Kan extension; left Kan extension is its left-adjoint counterpart.

Special adjoint functor theorem

Words: 195 Articles: 2
Adjoint functors OurBigBook.com
The colimit form of the Special adjoint functor theorem says that a colimit-preserving functor from a locally small, cocomplete, well-copowered category with a small generating family to a locally small category has a right adjoint.

Limit form of the special adjoint functor theorem

Words: 160 Articles: 1
Special adjoint functor theorem OurBigBook.com
A functor G:C→D from a locally small category that is complete and well-powered, with a small cogenerating family, to a locally small category has a left adjoint exactly when it preserves small categorical limits. For sufficiency, the cogenerator bound for comma-category solution sets produces a weakly initial set in each complete comma category (B↓G). The initial-object lemma for complete categories with a weakly initial set supplies its initial object, a universal arrow from an object to a functor. Necessity is limit preservation by a right adjoint.
Cogenerator bound for comma-category solution sets (C(C0​,Qi​)↪D(B,GQi​))
Words: 112
Limit form of the special adjoint functor theorem OurBigBook.com
Under the hypotheses of the limit form of the special adjoint functor theorem, intersect all subobjects of C supporting x:B→GC. Limit preservation gives a smallest supporting (C0​,x0​). If G(u)x0​=G(v)x0​ for maps u,v:C0​→Qi​, their equalizer supports x0​, so minimality makes it invertible and u=v. Thus the indicated map of hom-sets is injective. The evaluation embedding into cogenerator products embeds C0​ in a product of cogenerators indexed by the realized subsets of the fixed sets D(B,GQi​). There are only a set of such products, a set of their subobjects, and a set of maps from B into their images under G. These data give a weakly initial set in (B↓G). Using realized subsets avoids assuming maps into every cogenerator exist.

Cartesian closed category

Words: 1k Articles: 24
Adjoint functors OurBigBook.com
A category with finite products is cartesian closed when every product functor −×A has a right adjoint (−)A, called exponentiation by A.

Locally Cartesian closed category

Words: 37
Cartesian closed category OurBigBook.com
A category with finite limits is locally Cartesian closed when every slice category is a Cartesian closed category. Covariant set-valued functor categories on small categories have this property, using the equivalence between their slices and functor categories on categories of elements.

Cartesian closed monoid (M=End(D))

Words: 84
Cartesian closed category OurBigBook.com
A monoid encoding a one-object product and exponential structure: pairing is inverse to the map z↦(πz,π′z), and currying is inverse to y↦ε⟨yπ,π′⟩. These bijections imply pairing naturality ⟨x,y⟩z=⟨xz,yz⟩ and currying naturality (x⟨zπ,π′⟩)∗=x∗z. The element e=(π′)∗ then satisfies ez=e for every z, hence is idempotent. Splitting e supplies a terminal object and a two-object Cartesian closed category whose endomorphisms at the original object are M. For the original object to be nonterminal, M must be nontrivial.

Extensional reflexive object (D≅DD)

Words: 51
Cartesian closed category OurBigBook.com
An object isomorphic to its own exponential supplies mutually inverse folding and unfolding maps. Evaluation defines application, and folding after currying defines abstraction. The exponential universal property gives the beta rule, while the full isomorphism gives eta conversion. A mere retraction of the function object generally suffices for beta but not automatically eta.

Exponential object (BA)

Words: 408 Articles: 7
Cartesian closed category OurBigBook.com
An exponential object BA represents maps out of a product with A: there are natural bijections
C(X×A,B)≅C(X,BA).
(18)
The corresponding operations are currying and uncurrying, and the identity of BA corresponds to the evaluation morphism BA×A→B.
Exponential of covariant set-valued functors ((HG)(c)=Nat(C(c,−)×G,H))
Words: 58
Exponential object OurBigBook.com
For a small category, this formula defines the exponential object in its covariant set-valued functor category. An arrow c→d acts by precomposition with C(d,−)→C(c,−). Evaluation applies a natural transformation to (1c​,z); currying a map P×G→H sends p∈P(c) to the transformation (f,z)↦θ(P(f)p,z). The formulas prove the universal property directly, without an adjoint existence theorem.
Currying (h:Z×X→Y⟷h:Z→YX)
Words: 34
Exponential object OurBigBook.com
Currying transforms a morphism of two variables into a morphism taking values in an exponential object. The evaluation map of an exponential object recovers the original morphism. Its categorical universal property requires naturality and uniqueness, not just an underlying set bijection.
Evaluation map of an exponential object (ev:YX×X→Y)
Words: 46
Exponential object OurBigBook.com
The evaluation map is the counit representing application in an exponential object. For every Z, composition with evaluation gives the natural bijection Hom(Z,YX)≅Hom(Z×X,Y). Its inverse is currying. Evaluation must be a morphism in the ambient category, such as an equivariant map in a category of group actions.
Exponential of monoid sets (BA≅HomM​(M×A,B))
Words: 182 Articles: 2
Exponential object OurBigBook.com
For left M-sets, BA consists of equivariant maps of monoid sets M×A→B for the diagonal action on the domain. Its action is (m⋅f)(w,a)=f(wm,a) and evaluation is f(1,a). The curry of an equivariant h:C×A→B is h(c)(w,a)=h(w⋅c,a). This construction can have noninjective action maps even when both A and B are decidable.
Nondecidable exponential of decidable monoid sets
Words: 59
Exponential of monoid sets OurBigBook.com
For the free monoid on x,y, act on N by adding word length and on {0,1} trivially. Both actions are injective. The equivariant function f(w,n) indicating words of length strictly greater than n ending in x is nonzero, but y⋅f=0. Thus the exponential of monoid sets is not decidable. Strict inequality ensures invariance when the original word is empty.
Monoid condition for decidable exponentials (∀m ∃p,q: pmq=p)
Words: 69
Exponential of monoid sets OurBigBook.com
If each m admits p,q with pmq=p, then BA is decidable whenever the left M-set B is. For equivariant f,g, equality of all values at (1,a) implies equality at (m,a): apply p and use f(pm,pa)=pm⋅f(1,qa), then cancel the injective action of p on B. Equality after the exponential action of m then gives equal traces by cancelling its action on B.
Currying adjunction for small categories (−×C⊣[C,−])
Words: 46
Exponential object OurBigBook.com
A functor D×C→E is uniquely a functor D→[C,E]: fix its first coordinate and use its first-coordinate arrows as natural transformations. Uncurrying evaluates those transformations and second-coordinate arrows. The adjunction unit inserts a fixed first coordinate, and the adjunction counit is evaluation. This makes the category of small categories cartesian closed.

Exponential ideal

Words: 86 Articles: 1
Cartesian closed category OurBigBook.com
A full subcategory D of a Cartesian closed category C is an exponential ideal when BA belongs to D for every B∈D and every A∈C.
Reflector product criterion for an exponential ideal
Words: 58
Exponential ideal OurBigBook.com
For a reflective subcategory D of a Cartesian closed category C, with reflector L, the subcategory D is an exponential ideal if and only if the canonical comparison
L(A×B)⟶LA×LB
(19)
is an isomorphism for every A,B. The proof repeatedly curries a map into an object of D and factors it through the unit of the reflection.

Exponentiable object

Words: 222 Articles: 4
Cartesian closed category OurBigBook.com
An object X in a category with finite products is exponentiable when −×X has a right adjoint [X,−]. The terminal object is exponentiable, and exponentiable objects are closed under binary products because right adjoints compose:
[X×Y,−]≅[X,[Y,−]].
(20)
Exponentiability test using a coseparator (C(−×A,S) representable)
Words: 56
Exponentiable object OurBigBook.com
In a complete category that is a locally small category with a coseparator S and all monomorphisms regular, an object A is an exponentiable object exactly when C(−×A,S) is a representable functor. A representing object E gives representations EI for maps into powers SI. An equalizer presentation by powers of a coseparator then constructs a representation for maps into every target. The Yoneda lemma makes these representations functorial and supplies the right adjoint.
Product of exponentiable objects is exponentiable
Words: 35
Exponentiable object OurBigBook.com
If A and B are exponentiable objects, then
−×(A×B)≅(−×A)×B
(21)
has the composite of their exponential functors as a right adjoint. The terminal object supplies the empty product, so exponentiable objects are closed under finite products.
Zero object is the only exponentiable object in a pointed category
Words: 37
Exponentiable object OurBigBook.com
If the terminal object is also initial and E is exponentiable, the left adjoint −×E preserves the initial object. But 0×E≅E because 0 is terminal, while preservation of initiality gives 0×E≅0. Hence E≅0.
Exponentiability criterion in the category of T0 spaces (Top0​(−×E,S) representable)
Words: 55
Exponentiable object OurBigBook.com
A T0​ space E is exponentiable in Top0​ if and only if the functor Top0​(−×E,S) to sets is representable, where S is the Sierpiński space. Every T0​ space is an equalizer of maps between powers of S, so a representing object for maps into S constructs exponentials for every target by products and equalizers.

Cartesian closed category of posets

Words: 27
Cartesian closed category OurBigBook.com
The exponential BA in the category of posets is the poset of monotone maps A→B ordered pointwise. Evaluation is monotone, and currying gives the cartesian-closed adjunction.

Tiny object

Words: 246 Articles: 4
Cartesian closed category OurBigBook.com
An object A of a Cartesian closed category is tiny when exponentiation (−)A itself has a right adjoint.
The extra adjunction defining a tiny object should not be confused with the filtered-colimit condition for a compact object (mathematics).
Tiny covariant functor on a Cauchy-complete category with an initial object is representable
Words: 68
Tiny object OurBigBook.com
Let C be a small Cauchy-complete category with initial object 0. The terminal object of [C,Set] is h0​, so Nat(P,F)≅(FP)(0). If P is tiny, exponentiation by P is itself a left adjoint and preserves all colimits. Evaluation at zero also preserves colimits. Consequently Nat(P,−) preserves coproducts and epimorphisms, since every epimorphism in a set-valued functor category is the coequalizer of its kernel pair. Thus P is an irreducible projective in a set-valued functor category, hence representable.
Tiny covariant representable functor on a category with binary coproducts
Words: 46
Tiny object OurBigBook.com
For a small category C with binary coproducts, exponentiation by hA​=C(A,−) in [C,Set] is naturally F↦F(−⨿A): the exponential at B is Nat(hB​×hA​,F)≅Nat(hB⨿A​,F)≅F(B⨿A) by the Yoneda lemma. This precomposition functor has a right adjoint given by Right Kan extension, so hA​ is a tiny object.
Tiny objects are closed under finite products
Words: 47
Tiny object OurBigBook.com
In a Cartesian closed category, exponentiation satisfies (−)A×B≅((−)B)A. If the two exponential functors have right adjoints, their composite has the composite of those right adjoints in reverse order. Therefore a product of tiny objects is tiny. The terminal object is tiny since exponentiation by it is the identity, covering the empty product.
Representable presheaves are the tiny objects of an idempotent-complete finite-product category
Words: 52
Tiny object OurBigBook.com
If a small finite-product category C splits idempotents, the tiny objects of its presheaf topos are exactly the representable presheaves. Exponentiation by yA is precomposition with −×A and therefore has a right adjoint given by Right Kan extension. Conversely, if P is tiny, then Nat(P,−) preserves all colimits; idempotent completeness makes every such presheaf representable.

Category of metric spaces and non-expansive maps (Met)

Words: 174 Articles: 5
Category OurBigBook.com
The category Met has metric spaces as objects and maps f satisfying d(fx,fy)≤d(x,y) as morphisms. Its binary product uses the maximum metric.

Non-expansive map

Words: 15
Category of metric spaces and non-expansive maps OurBigBook.com
A non-expansive map between metric spaces is a function f such that d(fx,fy)≤d(x,y).

Category of bounded metric spaces and non-expansive maps (Metb​)

Words: 100 Articles: 2
Category of metric spaces and non-expansive maps OurBigBook.com
The category Metb​ is the full subcategory on bounded metric spaces. It has finite products: the terminal space is a singleton and
dX×Y​((x,y),(x′,y′))=max{dX​(x,x′),dY​(y,y′)}.
(22)

Metric exponential candidate ([X,Y])

Words: 75 Articles: 1
Category of bounded metric spaces and non-expansive maps OurBigBook.com
For bounded metric spaces X,Y, let [X,Y] be the set of non-expansive maps and define
dˉ(f,g)=sup{dY​(fx,gy):dX​(x,y)<dY​(fx,gy)}.
(23)
Whenever dˉ satisfies the triangle inequality, it is a metric and makes [X,−] right adjoint to −×X in Metb​.
Interpolating metric space
Words: 35
Metric exponential candidate OurBigBook.com
A metric space X is interpolating when d(x,y)=r+s implies that some z satisfies d(x,z)=r and d(z,y)=s. Interpolation makes the metric exponential candidate satisfy the triangle inequality, so every bounded interpolating metric space is an exponentiable object of Metb​.

Quotient metric

Words: 36
Category of metric spaces and non-expansive maps OurBigBook.com
The quotient metric is the largest metric on a quotient set for which the quotient map is non-expansive. It is obtained by taking infima of lengths of chains that may jump freely within equivalence classes.

Final functor

Words: 105 Articles: 2
Category OurBigBook.com
A functor F:C→D is final when every comma category (B↓F) is nonempty and connected. Colimits are unchanged after restriction along a final functor.

Finality of a functor (π0​(b↓F)=1 for every b)

Words: 24
Final functor OurBigBook.com
The finality property of a functor means every required comma category is nonempty and connected. It is the condition defining a final functor; the displayed criterion uses categorical connected components.

Cocone extension along a final functor

Words: 55
Final functor OurBigBook.com
Let F:I→J be final and D:J→C. A cocone λi​:D(Fi)→X extends uniquely to D: for j∈J, choose (i,u:j→Fi) in (j↓F) and set λˉj​=λi​D(u). Connectedness makes this independent of the choice. Consequently
colimi∈I​D(Fi)≅colimj∈J​D(j)
(24)
whenever either side is constructed by this universal property.

Discrete fibration

Words: 240 Articles: 5
Category OurBigBook.com
A functor F:C→D is a discrete fibration when every arrow B→FA has a unique lift with codomain A.

Unique lifting property of a discrete fibration

Words: 37
Discrete fibration OurBigBook.com
An incoming morphism into the image of a specified object has exactly one lift with that specified codomain. Both its source object and its lifted morphism are determined. Applying uniqueness to identity and composite morphisms gives the functoriality of lifting.

Orthogonality of final functors and discrete fibrations

Words: 55
Discrete fibration OurBigBook.com
Given a commutative square whose left functor is final and whose right functor is a discrete fibration, there is a unique diagonal functor filling the square. To construct its value on an object, choose an object of the relevant connected comma category and lift the resulting arrow; uniqueness of lifts makes the answer constant over that connected category.

Final-discrete-fibration factorization

Words: 126 Articles: 2
Discrete fibration OurBigBook.com
Every functor factors as a final functor followed by a discrete fibration. For F:C→D, the intermediate category has objects (B,c), where B∈D and c is a connected component of (B↓F). An arrow (B,c)→(B′,c′) is an arrow g:B→B′ whose precomposition functor sends c′ to c.

Uniqueness of a final-discrete-fibration factorization

Words: 36
Final-discrete-fibration factorization OurBigBook.com
Two factorizations of one functor have a unique connecting functor in each direction, by the orthogonality of final functors and discrete fibrations. Their composites and the identity fill the same lifting square, so uniqueness makes both composites identities. The intermediate categories are therefore canonically isomorphic.

Connected-component presheaf of a functor (B↦π0​(B↓F))

Words: 40
Final-discrete-fibration factorization OurBigBook.com
For a functor F:C→D, precomposition by u:B→B′ induces (B′↓F)→(B↓F), hence a map of categorical connected components in the opposite direction to u. This defines a presheaf on D. Its category of elements is the intermediate category in the final-discrete-fibration factorization.

Category of fields (Fld)

Words: 28
Category OurBigBook.com
The category of fields has fields as objects and unital field homomorphisms as morphisms. Every morphism is injective.
It is the full subcategory of the category of rings on field objects.

Compact object (mathematics)

Words: 21
Category OurBigBook.com
A compact object (mathematics) is an object whose represented Hom functor preserves filtered colimits. This preservation condition differs from the extra right-adjoint property defining a tiny object.
